entries.subject: USGS Iapetus Cassini–Voyager 783 m mosaic
entries.finding: Iapetus_Cassini_Voyager_mosaic_global_783m.tif supplies Monochrome; its native coverage, zero gaps, seams and photographed shadows remain.

entries.subject: NASA/JPL PIA18436 2014 enhanced-color map
entries.finding: The 11,741 by 5,871 calibrated, registered Cassini map supplies Enhanced color. Ultraviolet/infrared bands extend beyond human vision, so it is not natural color.

entries.subject: Cassini VIMS C1568129671_1 IR cube
entries.finding: The accepted calibrated cube, navigation cube and detector data are the primary source for false-color Infrared and continuum-relative Ice absorption; native support and archive filtering define coverage.

entries.subject: Iapetus VIMS absolute pointing
entries.finding: Native support and aperture checks do not establish exact absolute pointing; a missing background row and its filtering dependencies are withheld.
entries.revisitWhen: Independent controls qualify absolute source-camera registration.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Squyres et al. (1984) found a lunar-like law (Lommel-Seeliger, which has no parameter) adequate for Voyager images at 8 to 90 degrees phase, with a phase function that varies with albedo. Only the abstract could be read, so the emission range and the phase function are unknown. Iapetus keeps the shared sphere bank.
entries.revisitWhen: The fitted emission range of Squyres et al. (1984), or a Cassini disc-resolved Iapetus law with its ranges, is read in the paper.
